commands.name: 3DALIGN
commands.description: Aligns objects with other objects in 3D space using source and destination points.
commands.example: Select objects, then specify source and destination point pairs.
commands.tips: Use the Scale option when the target geometry is a different size.

commands.name: 3DARRAY
commands.description: Creates rectangular, polar, or path arrays in 3D.
commands.example: Select 3D objects and choose array type and count.
commands.tips: Path arrays follow splines, polylines, or helixes.

commands.name: 3DFACE
commands.description: Creates a three- or four-sided 3D surface face.
commands.example: Pick three or four corner points in order.
commands.tips: Legacy surface tool; mesh and surface tools are more flexible today.

commands.name: 3DMESH
commands.description: Creates a 3D mesh surface from a grid of vertices.
commands.example: Enter M and N mesh size, then vertex heights.
commands.tips: Legacy tool; MESH commands are more flexible today.

commands.name: 3DMIRROR
commands.description: Mirrors 3D objects across a defined mirror plane.
commands.example: Select objects and define three points for the mirror plane.
commands.tips: Helpful for symmetric mechanical parts and architectural masses.

commands.name: 3DMOVE
commands.description: Moves selected objects in 3D using a gizmo or specified displacement.
commands.example: Select objects and drag axis handles or enter a displacement.
commands.tips: Combine with Ortho and snap modes for precise relocations.

commands.name: 3DORBIT
commands.description: Rotates the view in 3D space interactively.
commands.example: Drag to orbit; Shift for horizontal, Ctrl for roll.
commands.tips: Use ViewCube for quick preset orientations.

commands.name: 3DPRINT
commands.description: Sends 3D solids to a connected printing service.
commands.example: Select solids and confirm print settings.
commands.tips: Verify units before sending to a printer.

commands.name: 3DROTATE
commands.description: Rotates objects in 3D about an axis you define.
commands.example: Select objects, pick a base point, then define rotation axis and angle.
commands.tips: Use reference option to align geometry to existing edges.

commands.name: 3DSCALE
commands.description: Scales objects uniformly or non-uniformly in 3D space.
commands.example: Select objects and adjust scale along X, Y, and Z.
commands.tips: Non-uniform scaling can distort blocks; explode first if needed.

commands.name: 3DWALK
commands.description: Navigates a perspective view as if walking through the model.
commands.example: Open walk mode and use keyboard or mouse controls to move.
commands.tips: Set eye height for realistic architectural walkthroughs.

commands.name: ABOUT
commands.description: Displays product version and license information.
commands.example: Run to view application about dialog.
commands.tips: Verify version when troubleshooting compatibility.

commands.name: ADCENTER
commands.description: Opens DesignCenter to access drawings, blocks, layers, and layouts.
commands.example: Browse folders and drag content into the current drawing.
commands.tips: Save time by reusing details from your office standard library.

commands.name: ADDSELECTED
commands.description: Creates a new object using the same properties and type as a selected object.
commands.example: Select source object, then place the new object.
commands.tips: Speeds up repetitive drafting when matching an existing entity.

commands.name: AI_BOX
commands.description: Creates a 3D solid box using the classic primitive workflow.
commands.example: Specify corner points and height.
commands.tips: BOX command offers the same capability with modern prompts.

commands.name: AI_CONE
commands.description: Creates a 3D cone primitive from base and height values.
commands.example: Define base center, radius, and height.
commands.tips: Use CONE for the current equivalent tool.

commands.name: AI_CYL
commands.description: Creates a 3D cylinder primitive.
commands.example: Specify base, radius, and height.
commands.tips: CYLINDER is the modern matching command.

commands.name: AI_DISH
commands.description: Creates a dish-shaped 3D solid.
commands.example: Specify base and depth parameters.
commands.tips: Legacy primitive for bowl-like forms.

commands.name: AI_DOME
commands.description: Creates a dome-shaped 3D solid.
commands.example: Define base circle and dome height.
commands.tips: Legacy primitive; REVOLVE can model similar shapes.

commands.name: AI_PYRAMID
commands.description: Creates a 3D pyramid primitive.
commands.example: Set sides, base, and height.
commands.tips: PYRAMID command replaces this workflow.

commands.name: AI_SPHERE
commands.description: Creates a 3D sphere primitive.
commands.example: Pick center and radius.
commands.tips: SPHERE provides the same result.

commands.name: AI_TORUS
commands.description: Creates a 3D torus primitive.
commands.example: Define center, torus radius, and tube radius.
commands.tips: Use TORUS in current workflows.

commands.name: AI_WEDGE
commands.description: Creates a 3D wedge primitive.
commands.example: Specify base rectangle and height.
commands.tips: WEDGE is the modern equivalent.

commands.name: ALIASEDIT
commands.description: Edits command alias definitions in the acad.pgp file.
commands.example: Modify shortcut to command mappings.
commands.tips: Customize keyboard shortcuts for speed.

commands.name: ALIGN
commands.description: Aligns objects with other objects in 2D and 3D.
commands.example: Select objects → source point(s) → destination point(s).
commands.tips: Scale objects during alignment by choosing Yes when prompted.

commands.name: ALIGNSPACE
commands.description: Aligns layout viewports to match each other.
commands.example: Select viewports and alignment points.
commands.tips: Coordinates plan and enlarged plan views.

commands.name: APPLOAD
commands.description: Loads and manages external application routines and LISP files.
commands.example: Browse to ARX, VLX, or LSP files and load at startup if needed.
commands.tips: Only load trusted customizations from known sources.

commands.name: ARC
commands.description: Creates an arc defined by three points, start/center/end, or other methods.
commands.example: 3-point arc: start → second point → end point.
commands.tips: Hold Ctrl to switch arc direction while specifying points.

commands.name: ARCTEXT
commands.description: Aligns text along an arc curve.
commands.example: Select arc and enter text content.
commands.tips: Express tool for curved labels.

commands.name: AREA
commands.description: Calculates the area and perimeter of objects or defined areas.
commands.example: Object option for closed shapes, or Add/Subtract points.
commands.tips: Use for takeoffs and verifying hatch boundaries.

commands.name: ARRAY
commands.description: Creates copies of objects in a rectangular, polar, or path pattern.
commands.example: Select objects → choose Rectangular, Polar, or Path array.
commands.tips: Associative arrays can be edited after creation from the ribbon.

commands.name: ARRAYCLASSIC
commands.description: Creates arrays using the classic dialog workflow.
commands.example: Select objects and define array pattern.
commands.tips: Use ARRAY for modern associative arrays.

commands.name: ATTDEF
commands.description: Defines attribute characteristics within a block.
commands.example: Tag → prompt → default value → placement.
commands.tips: Use ATTEDIT or EATTEDIT to modify block attributes later.

commands.name: ATTDISP
commands.description: Controls visibility of block attribute values.
commands.example: Set Normal, On, or Off display mode.
commands.tips: Hide attributes temporarily without deleting them.

commands.name: ATTEDIT
commands.description: Edits attribute values in block references individually.
commands.example: Select block and update tag values in the dialog.
commands.tips: EATTEDIT supports batch editing of multiple block attributes.

commands.name: ATTEXT
commands.description: Exports block attribute values to an external file.
commands.example: Choose format and select blocks.
commands.tips: DATAEXTRACTION offers more export options.

commands.name: ATTIPEDIT
commands.description: Edits block attribute text in place on screen.
commands.example: Double-click attribute text to edit.
commands.tips: Fast title block and tag updates.

commands.name: ATTREQ
commands.description: Controls whether attribute values are prompted during INSERT.
commands.example: Set to 1 to prompt, 0 to use defaults.
commands.tips: Speed up insertion when defaults are fine.

commands.name: ATTSYNC
commands.description: Synchronizes block attribute definitions with existing block references.
commands.example: Select block name to update all instances.
commands.tips: Run after editing attribute definitions in a block.

commands.name: AUDIT
commands.description: Evaluates and fixes errors in a drawing file.
commands.example: Type Y to fix detected errors.
commands.tips: Run on files that crash or behave unexpectedly.

commands.name: BACTION
commands.description: Adds an action to a dynamic block parameter.
commands.example: Select parameter and affected objects.
commands.tips: Build dynamic blocks inside BEDIT.

commands.name: BACTIONBAR
commands.description: Shows or hides dynamic block action bars.
commands.example: Select block reference and toggle bar.
commands.tips: Hide bars for cleaner plotted output.

commands.name: BATTMAN
commands.description: Manages attribute definitions within a block definition.
commands.example: Open block, reorder or edit attribute properties.
commands.tips: Use before ATTSYNC to push changes to references.

commands.name: BCLOSE
commands.description: Closes the block editor and saves or discards changes.
commands.example: Choose Save or Discard after editing a block.
commands.tips: Saving updates every instance of that block.

commands.name: BCOUNT
commands.description: Counts block instances and reports totals in the text window.
commands.example: Select blocks or count entire drawing.
commands.tips: Text-window alternative to COUNT command.

commands.name: BEDIT
commands.description: Opens the block editor to modify block geometry and constraints.
commands.example: Select a block definition and edit in the temporary editor environment.
commands.tips: Use BCLOSE and save changes to update all block instances.

commands.name: BHATCH
commands.description: Opens hatch creation using the classic boundary hatch workflow.
commands.example: Define pick points or select objects for hatch boundary.
commands.tips: Functionally similar to HATCH with dialog-driven options.

commands.name: BIND
commands.description: Converts xref dependencies into permanent block definitions.
commands.example: Select xref and choose Bind or Insert conversion type.
commands.tips: Insert adds block names with prefix; Bind removes xref link.

commands.name: BLEND
commands.description: Creates a tangent fillet between two 2D lines or curves.
commands.example: Select first object → second object.
commands.tips: Smooth transitions between non-parallel linework.

commands.name: BLOCK
commands.description: Creates a block definition from selected objects.
commands.example: Name → base point → select objects.
commands.tips: Choose Convert to Block to replace geometry with an instance.

commands.name: BLOCKREPLACE
commands.description: Replaces one block reference with another globally.
commands.example: Select source and destination block names.
commands.tips: Express tool for symbol standardization.

commands.name: BLOOKUPTABLE
commands.description: Creates lookup tables for dynamic block states.
commands.example: Define lookup properties and visibility states.
commands.tips: One block can represent many symbol variants.

commands.name: BMOD
commands.description: Opens the Block Editor for a selected block reference.
commands.example: Select block and edit definition in place.
commands.tips: Shortcut workflow similar to BEDIT.

commands.name: BOUNDARY
commands.description: Creates a region or polyline from an enclosed area.
commands.example: Pick an internal point within a closed area.
commands.tips: If boundary fails, gaps may exist—use BPOLY gap tolerance.

commands.name: BOX
commands.description: Creates a 3D solid box from a base rectangle and height.
commands.example: First corner → opposite corner → height.
commands.tips: Use Center option when aligning to a known midpoint.

commands.name: BPARAMETER
commands.description: Adds a parameter to a dynamic block definition.
commands.example: Choose parameter type and placement.
commands.tips: Parameters create grips on block inserts.

commands.name: BPOLY
commands.description: Creates a polyline boundary around an internal pick point.
commands.example: Pick an internal point inside a closed area.
commands.tips: Increase gap tolerance if the boundary fails to detect.

commands.name: BREAK
commands.description: Breaks an object between two points.
commands.example: Select object → first break point → second break point.
commands.tips: Use @ for a single-point break at the pick location.

commands.name: BREAKLINE
commands.description: Creates a break-line symbol at a chosen location.
commands.example: Specify break point and symbol size.
commands.tips: Common for shortened views in details.

commands.name: BREP
commands.description: Converts a 3D solid to a boundary representation form.
commands.example: Select solid objects to convert.
commands.tips: Used in advanced solid exchange workflows.

commands.name: BSAVE
commands.description: Saves the current block editor session.
commands.example: Run while editing a block to save changes.
commands.tips: Use BCLOSE when finished editing.

commands.name: BURST
commands.description: Explodes a block while preserving attribute values as text.
commands.example: Select block references to burst into geometry and text.
commands.tips: Handy when converting legacy blocks to plain geometry.

commands.name: BVMODE
commands.description: Controls visibility of dynamic block parameter frames.
commands.example: Toggle parameter display in block editor.
commands.tips: Turn off when frames clutter the block.

commands.name: CAL
commands.description: Evaluates mathematical and geometric expressions at the command line.
commands.example: Enter expressions using points, vectors, and functions.
commands.tips: Useful for transparent calculations during active commands.

commands.name: CAMERA
commands.description: Creates a named camera object for 3D views and rendering.
commands.example: Specify camera location and target point.
commands.tips: Save camera views for consistent presentation shots.

commands.name: CELTSCALE
commands.description: Sets the linetype scale for newly created objects.
commands.example: Enter object linetype scale at the command line.
commands.tips: Use when one object needs a denser or sparser linetype pattern.

commands.name: CENTERLINE
commands.description: Creates associative centerlines between pairs of lines or arcs.
commands.example: Pick two lines or arcs to generate a centerline.
commands.tips: Use CENTERMARK for holes and circular features.

commands.name: CENTERMARK
commands.description: Creates an associative center mark on circles or arcs.
commands.example: Select a circle or arc to place the mark.
commands.tips: Adjust extension length in the center mark style.

commands.name: CHAMFER
commands.description: Bevels the corners of two objects by a specified distance.
commands.example: Set distances → select first line → select second line.
commands.tips: Use Distance and Angle method for asymmetric chamfers.

commands.name: CHAMFEREDGE
commands.description: Bevels edges on a 3D solid.
commands.example: Select edges and enter chamfer distances.
commands.tips: Apply to multiple edges at once.

commands.name: CHANGE
commands.description: Changes properties of selected objects at the command line.
commands.example: Select objects and respond to property prompts.
commands.tips: Older workflow; PROPERTIES palette covers most use cases today.

commands.name: CHECKSTANDARDS
commands.description: Checks drawing objects against CAD standards.
commands.example: Run audit and review violations list.
commands.tips: Enforce office layer and style rules.

commands.name: CHPROP
commands.description: Changes the color, layer, linetype, and other properties of objects.
commands.example: Select objects → answer prompts for new properties.
commands.tips: PROPERTIES palette is often faster for mixed edits.

commands.name: CHSPACE
commands.description: Moves selected objects between model space and paper space.
commands.example: Select objects in a viewport or layout and run CHSPACE.
commands.tips: Scale may change; verify dimensions after moving between spaces.

commands.name: CHSPACEX
commands.description: Advanced object transfer between model and paper space.
commands.example: Select objects to change space context.
commands.tips: Express tool variant of CHSPACE.

commands.name: CIRCLE
commands.description: Creates a circle defined by center point and radius.
commands.example: Center point → radius, or D for diameter, 2P for two points, 3P for three points.
commands.tips: Use TTR (tangent-tangent-radius) for circles tangent to two objects.

commands.name: CLIPIT
commands.description: Clips blocks, xrefs, and images with a polyline boundary.
commands.example: Select reference and clipping polyline.
commands.tips: Express tool alternative to XCLIP.

commands.name: CLOSE
commands.description: Closes the current drawing.
commands.example: Type CLOSE and save changes if prompted.
commands.tips: Use CLOSEALL to shut every open drawing at once.

commands.name: CLOSEALL
commands.description: Closes all open drawings in the session.
commands.example: Confirm save prompts for each modified file.
commands.tips: Useful at the end of a work session to avoid unsaved tabs.

commands.name: CMDECHO
commands.description: Controls whether commands echo to the text window during scripts.
commands.example: Set to 0 to suppress echo in scripts.
commands.tips: Useful when running SCR files.

commands.name: COLOR
commands.description: Sets the default color for new objects.
commands.example: Pick color index or true color from the dialog.
commands.tips: ByLayer color is recommended for standards-based workflows.

commands.name: COMPARE
commands.description: Compares two drawings and highlights differences.
commands.example: Select baseline and comparison files.
commands.tips: Speeds revision review workflows.

commands.name: CONE
commands.description: Creates a 3D solid cone with circular or elliptical base.
commands.example: Base center → base radius → height or apex point.
commands.tips: Top radius option creates truncated cones.

commands.name: CONVTOMESH
commands.description: Converts solids, surfaces, or legacy mesh types to mesh objects.
commands.example: Select objects and set mesh smoothness.
commands.tips: Required before some mesh editing operations.

commands.name: CONVTONURBS
commands.description: Converts eligible objects to NURBS surfaces.
commands.example: Select solids or surfaces to convert.
commands.tips: Use when downstream tools require NURBS data.

commands.name: CONVTOSOLID
commands.description: Converts eligible surfaces, meshes, or profiles into 3D solids.
commands.example: Select objects and confirm conversion options.
commands.tips: Clean geometry converts more reliably than open surfaces.

commands.name: CONVTOSURFACE
commands.description: Converts eligible objects into procedural surfaces.
commands.example: Select objects to convert and review settings.
commands.tips: Use when preparing objects for surface editing tools.

commands.name: COPY
commands.description: Duplicates selected objects to a new location.
commands.example: Select objects → base point → displacement point. Type M for multiple copies.
commands.tips: Use Array mode for rectangular or polar arrays from the COPY command options.

commands.name: COPYBASE
commands.description: Copies selected objects to the clipboard with a base point.
commands.example: Specify base point, then select objects.
commands.tips: Use with PASTECLIP for precise placement in another file.

commands.name: COPYCLIP
commands.description: Copies selected objects to the system clipboard.
commands.example: Select objects and run COPYCLIP.
commands.tips: Use PASTEORIG to paste at the same coordinates in another file.

commands.name: COPYLINK
commands.description: Copies drawing objects with a link to the source file.
commands.example: Select objects and destination application.
commands.tips: Legacy OLE linking workflow.

commands.name: COPYM
commands.description: Copies objects multiple times with interactive placement.
commands.example: Select objects and place repeated copies.
commands.tips: Express tool for quick duplication.

commands.name: COPYNESTED
commands.description: Copies objects nested inside blocks or xrefs.
commands.example: Select nested object and new location.
commands.tips: Similar workflow to NCOPY.

commands.name: COPYTOLAYER
commands.description: Copies objects to another layer while optionally keeping the original.
commands.example: Select objects and destination layer.
commands.tips: Useful for duplicating geometry onto detail layers.

commands.name: COUNT
commands.description: Counts block instances and displays totals in the drawing area.
commands.example: Select blocks to count or count entire drawing.
commands.tips: Add field tags for live-updating quantity schedules.

commands.name: CUSTOMIZE
commands.description: Edits user interface elements such as ribbons, menus, and toolbars.
commands.example: Drag commands to workspaces and save a custom CUIx file.
commands.tips: Export workspace backups before major UI changes.

commands.name: CUTCLIP
commands.description: Copies selected objects to the clipboard and erases them.
commands.example: Select objects to cut.
commands.tips: Equivalent to Cut in many editing workflows.

commands.name: CVPORT
commands.description: Sets the active viewport number in tiled model space or layouts.
commands.example: Enter viewport number to make active.
commands.tips: Useful in scripts that target a specific viewport.

commands.name: CYLINDER
commands.description: Creates a 3D solid cylinder or elliptical cylinder.
commands.example: Base center → radius → height.
commands.tips: Use Axis endpoint option when the cylinder is not vertical.

commands.name: DATAEXTRACTION
commands.description: Extracts object properties into tables or external files.
commands.example: Create new extraction, choose objects, select properties, output table.
commands.tips: Build door and window schedules directly from block attributes.

commands.name: DATE
commands.description: Displays the current date and time.
commands.example: Run to view system date in text window.
commands.tips: Useful when documenting session notes.

commands.name: DELCONSTRAINT
commands.description: Removes geometric constraints from selected objects.
commands.example: Select constrained geometry.
commands.tips: Use when constraints block needed edits.

commands.name: DETACH
commands.description: Removes an xref from the current drawing.
commands.example: Select xref name to detach.
commands.tips: Does not delete the external file from disk.

commands.name: DGNATTACH
commands.description: Attaches a MicroStation DGN file as an underlay reference.
commands.example: Choose DGN file, design model, and placement settings.
commands.tips: Common in civil and infrastructure coordination workflows.

commands.name: DGNCLIP
commands.description: Clips a DGN underlay to a specified boundary.
commands.example: Select DGN underlay and set clip area.
commands.tips: Common in civil coordination workflows.

commands.name: DGNEXPORT
commands.description: Exports the drawing to MicroStation DGN format.
commands.example: Choose version and export options.
commands.tips: Common for civil infrastructure exchange.

commands.name: DGNIMPORT
commands.description: Imports a DGN file into the current drawing.
commands.example: Select file and layer mapping.
commands.tips: Verify units after import.

commands.name: DIGITALSIGN
commands.description: Applies a digital signature to the drawing file.
commands.example: Select certificate and sign drawing.
commands.tips: Used for authenticated submittals.

commands.name: DIMALIGNED
commands.description: Creates a dimension aligned with the distance between two points.
commands.example: First point → second point → dimension line location.
commands.tips: Best choice when measuring angled distances along an object.

commands.name: DIMANGULAR
commands.description: Creates an angular dimension between lines, arcs, or three points.
commands.example: Select two lines or specify vertex and two sides.
commands.tips: Use arc option when dimensioning the included angle of an arc segment.

commands.name: DIMARC
commands.description: Creates an arc length dimension.
commands.example: Select an arc and place the dimension.
commands.tips: Use when the measured distance follows a curved edge.

commands.name: DIMBASELINE
commands.description: Creates a series of dimensions from a common baseline.
commands.example: Create a linear dimension first, then run DIMBASELINE for additional offsets.
commands.tips: Spacing is controlled by the current dimension style baseline offset.

commands.name: DIMBREAK
commands.description: Breaks dimension and multileader lines where they cross objects.
commands.example: Select dimension and object causing overlap.
commands.tips: Keeps crowded drawings readable without moving dimensions.

commands.name: DIMCENTER
commands.description: Creates center marks for arcs and circles.
commands.example: Select arc or circle to place center mark.
commands.tips: Use DIMDIAMETER or DIMRADIUS for size callouts in addition to center marks.

commands.name: DIMCONSTRAINT
commands.description: Applies dimensional constraints that drive geometry size.
commands.example: Select objects and enter constraint value.
commands.tips: Changing the value updates linked geometry.

commands.name: DIMCONTINUE
commands.description: Continues dimensions from the end of an existing dimension line.
commands.example: Start from a finished linear dimension, then pick subsequent points.
commands.tips: Useful for chained dimensions across repeated features.

commands.name: DIMDIAMETER
commands.description: Creates a diameter dimension for arcs and circles.
commands.example: Select arc or circle, then place the dimension.
commands.tips: Common for mechanical drawings where diameter is the primary notation.

commands.name: DIMDISASSOCIATE
commands.description: Breaks associativity between dimensions and geometry.
commands.example: Select associative dimensions.
commands.tips: Use before moving dimensions independently.

commands.name: DIMEDIT
commands.description: Edits dimension text, angle, and home position.
commands.example: Select dimensions and choose text or angle options.
commands.tips: Override text with measured value plus tolerance notes.

commands.name: DIMENSION
commands.description: Creates associative dimensions for distances, angles, and radii.
commands.example: Choose Linear, Aligned, Angular, or other dimension types from the ribbon.
commands.tips: Use DIMSTYLE to control arrow size, text height, and units.

commands.name: DIMINSPECT
commands.description: Adds or removes inspection frames on dimension text.
commands.example: Select dimensions and toggle inspection format.
commands.tips: Used in quality-control documentation.

commands.name: DIMJOGGED
commands.description: Creates a jogged radius dimension for small arcs.
commands.example: Select arc or circle, then place the jog and text.
commands.tips: Keeps large radius dimensions readable in tight views.

commands.name: DIMLINEAR
commands.description: Creates a linear dimension aligned with horizontal or vertical axes.
commands.example: First extension line origin → second origin → dimension line location.
commands.tips: Use DIMROTATED when the dimension line must follow an angled direction.

commands.name: DIMORDINATE
commands.description: Creates ordinate X or Y dimensions from a datum.
commands.example: Select feature point and place the dimension.
commands.tips: Common in CNC and machining drawings.

commands.name: DIMOVERRIDE
commands.description: Sets local overrides for dimension variables.
commands.example: Select dimensions and override settings.
commands.tips: Clear overrides to restore dimension style.

commands.name: DIMRADIUS
commands.description: Creates a radius dimension for arcs and circles.
commands.example: Select arc or circle, then place the dimension.
commands.tips: Switch to DIMDIAMETER when a diameter callout is required.

commands.name: DIMREASSOCIATE
commands.description: Reassociates dimensions with objects after geometry changes.
commands.example: Select non-associative dimensions to rebuild links.
commands.tips: Run after importing or exploding geometry.

commands.name: DIMROTATED
commands.description: Creates a linear dimension aligned with a specified rotation angle.
commands.example: Pick two points and set dimension line angle.
commands.tips: Use when the dimension line must not be horizontal or vertical.

commands.name: DIMSPACE
commands.description: Adjusts equal spacing between a series of dimensions.
commands.example: Select base dimension, then others in the set.
commands.tips: Cleans crowded dimension strings quickly.

commands.name: DIMSTYLE
commands.description: Creates and edits styles that control dimension appearance.
commands.example: Open the dimension style manager and set text, arrows, and units.
commands.tips: Keep one drawing standard per project to avoid mixed styles.

commands.name: DIMTEDIT
commands.description: Moves and rotates dimension text independently.
commands.example: Select dimension text and drag to a new location.
commands.tips: Double-click dimension text for quick in-place editing.

commands.name: DIST
commands.description: Measures the distance and angle between two points.
commands.example: First point → second point.
commands.tips: Results appear on the command line and in the MeasureGeom tool.

commands.name: DISTRIBUTE
commands.description: Evenly spaces objects between two points.
commands.example: Select objects and distribution endpoints.
commands.tips: Handy for equal spacing of fixtures or columns.

commands.name: DIVIDE
commands.description: Places point objects at equal intervals along an object.
commands.example: Select object → number of segments.
commands.tips: Use MEASURE for spacing at exact distance intervals.

commands.name: DLINE
commands.description: Creates double parallel lines using a dedicated tool.
commands.example: Pick points to draw double-line paths.
commands.tips: MLINE is the modern replacement.

commands.name: DONUT
commands.description: Creates a filled ring or circle.
commands.example: Inside diameter → outside diameter → center point.
commands.tips: Set inside diameter to 0 for a filled circle.

commands.name: DRAWORDER
commands.description: Changes the display order of overlapping objects.
commands.example: Select objects → choose Bring to Front, Send to Back, or relative options.
commands.tips: Hatch display issues are often fixed by sending hatch behind geometry.

commands.name: DSETTINGS
commands.description: Sets drafting aids including snap, polar tracking, and object snap tracking.
commands.example: Enable polar tracking angles and object snap tracking options.
commands.tips: F10 toggles polar tracking; F11 toggles object snap tracking.

commands.name: DVIEW
commands.description: Defines parallel or perspective viewing direction using camera targets.
commands.example: Select objects and define camera and target points.
commands.tips: Older camera tool; CAM VIEW and VIEW commands offer more control.

commands.name: DWFATTACH
commands.description: Attaches a DWF or DWFx file as an underlay.
commands.example: Choose file, sheet, and insertion parameters.
commands.tips: Useful for coordinating published sets from other teams.

commands.name: DWFCLIP
commands.description: Clips the visible region of a DWF underlay.
commands.example: Select underlay and define clip boundary.
commands.tips: Reduce clutter when only part of a sheet is needed.

commands.name: DWGCOMPARE
commands.description: Compares the current drawing with another to highlight differences.
commands.example: Select comparison drawing and review change overlays.
commands.tips: Use during revision review to spot moved or changed geometry.

commands.name: DWGCONVERT
commands.description: Batch converts drawings to another DWG version.
commands.example: Add files and target format version.
commands.tips: Prepare files for older software versions.

commands.name: DXFIN
commands.description: Imports drawing exchange format data into the current file.
commands.example: Select DXF file to import.
commands.tips: Check units and layers after import.

commands.name: DXFOUT
commands.description: Exports selected objects or the entire drawing to DXF format.
commands.example: Choose objects and destination file.
commands.tips: Use when sharing geometry with non-DWG applications.

commands.name: DYNMODE
commands.description: Controls dynamic input display at the cursor.
commands.example: Set to 0 off, 1 pointer input, 2 dimensional input, or 3 both.
commands.tips: F12 toggles dynamic input during drafting.

commands.name: EATTEDIT
commands.description: Edits attributes in selected block references with an enhanced dialog.
commands.example: Select blocks and modify attribute fields in a table view.
commands.tips: Use for title block revisions and equipment tag updates.

commands.name: EDGE
commands.description: Shows or hides edges on 3D surfaces and solids.
commands.example: Select edges and visibility option.
commands.tips: Hide interior edges for cleaner shaded views.

commands.name: EDGESURF
commands.description: Creates a surface bounded by four connected edges.
commands.example: Select edges in order around the boundary.
commands.tips: Edges must form a closed loop for predictable results.

commands.name: ELEV
commands.description: Sets default elevation and extrusion thickness for new objects.
commands.example: Enter elevation and thickness values.
commands.tips: Less common with modern 3D workflows.

commands.name: ELLIPSE
commands.description: Creates an ellipse or elliptical arc.
commands.example: Center → axis endpoint → other axis distance.
commands.tips: Use Arc option for partial elliptical arcs.

commands.name: ERASE
commands.description: Removes objects from the drawing.
commands.example: Select objects → Enter.
commands.tips: Use OOPS immediately after to restore the last erased set.

commands.name: ETRANSMIT
commands.description: Creates a transmittal package with drawings and related support files.
commands.example: Select files and configure package options.
commands.tips: Include fonts and xrefs when sending sets to consultants.

commands.name: EXOFFSET
commands.description: Offsets objects with extended options.
commands.example: Select object and offset distance.
commands.tips: Express tool variant of OFFSET.

commands.name: EXPLODE
commands.description: Breaks a compound object into its component objects.
commands.example: Select blocks, polylines, or dimensions to explode.
commands.tips: Exploding a block loses attribute information unless preserved.

commands.name: EXPORT
commands.description: Exports the drawing to another file format such as PDF or DWF.
commands.example: Choose format, path, and export options.
commands.tips: PDF export is common for client review sets.

commands.name: EXPORTLAYOUT
commands.description: Exports a layout tab to model space or a new file.
commands.example: Choose layout and destination.
commands.tips: Flatten sheet content for sharing.

commands.name: EXPORTPDF
commands.description: Exports selected layouts to PDF.
commands.example: Pick sheets and output folder.
commands.tips: Often faster than legacy plot-to-PDF.

commands.name: EXTEND
commands.description: Extends objects to meet the edges of boundary edges.
commands.example: Select boundary edges → select objects to extend.
commands.tips: Hold Shift while trimming to switch to Extend mode quickly.

commands.name: EXTRUDE
commands.description: Extends a 2D object into 3D space to create a solid or surface.
commands.example: Select profile → height or path.
commands.tips: Use Taper angle for drafted extrusions.

commands.name: FACETRES
commands.description: Adjusts smoothness of shaded and rendered curved surfaces.
commands.example: Enter facet resolution value between 0.01 and 10.
commands.tips: Increase for smoother 3D display; decrease for speed.

commands.name: FASTEXT
commands.description: Extends objects to meet boundaries quickly.
commands.example: Select objects to extend.
commands.tips: Express tool for rapid cleanup.

commands.name: FASTTRIM
commands.description: Trims objects quickly without selecting cutting edges first.
commands.example: Select objects to trim.
commands.tips: Express tool for fast editing sessions.

commands.name: FIELD
commands.description: Inserts a text field that updates from drawing properties.
commands.example: Choose field category such as date, plot scale, or object data.
commands.tips: Use fields in title blocks for automatic sheet values.

commands.name: FIELDEVAL
commands.description: Controls when fields are evaluated and updated.
commands.example: Set evaluation timing bitmask value.
commands.tips: Adjust if fields seem stale on plot.

commands.name: FILEDIA
commands.description: Toggles file dialog boxes for open and save commands.
commands.example: Set to 1 for dialogs, 0 for command line.
commands.tips: Set to 0 in automation scripts.

commands.name: FILL
commands.description: Controls solid fill display for hatches, solids, and wide polylines.
commands.example: Set fill mode on or off at the command line.
commands.tips: Turn off temporarily to speed up complex drawings.

commands.name: FILLET
commands.description: Rounds or fillets the corners of two objects with a specified radius.
commands.example: Set radius → select first line → select second line.
commands.tips: Set radius to 0 for a sharp corner trim/extend.

commands.name: FILLETEDGE
commands.description: Rounds edges on a 3D solid with a radius.
commands.example: Select edges and specify radius.
commands.tips: Small radii may fail on tight geometry.

commands.name: FILTER
commands.description: Defines and reuses selection filters for complex object queries.
commands.example: Build criteria by object type, color, layer, or linetype.
commands.tips: Save filters when you repeat the same selection workflow often.

commands.name: FIND
commands.description: Finds and optionally replaces specified text strings.
commands.example: Enter search text, replacement text, and search scope.
commands.tips: Use whole word and match case options for precise batch updates.

commands.name: FLATSHOT
commands.description: Projects a 3D view into a 2D block for documentation.
commands.example: Set viewpoint, export hidden lines to a new block.
commands.tips: Useful for quick 2D documentation from existing 3D geometry.

commands.name: FLATTEN
commands.description: Projects geometry to a uniform elevation.
commands.example: Select objects and confirm flatten.
commands.tips: Express tool for 2D cleanup of 3D exports.

commands.name: GCON
commands.description: Applies geometric constraints between objects.
commands.example: Select objects and constraint type.
commands.tips: Maintains design intent in parametric drawings.

commands.name: GEOATTACH
commands.description: Attaches geographic map data as a geolocation reference.
commands.example: Define location and import map imagery.
commands.tips: Requires geolocation setup for real-world coordinates.

commands.name: GEOGRAPHICLOCATION
commands.description: Sets geographic coordinates and north direction.
commands.example: Enter coordinates or pick from map.
commands.tips: Required for geolocation map workflows.

commands.name: GEOMAP
commands.description: Displays an online map under the drawing for geolocation context.
commands.example: Choose map type and capture area.
commands.tips: Internet connection required for map imagery.

commands.name: GEOMARK
commands.description: Marks and labels measured geometry such as distance or radius.
commands.example: Measure a value and place a labeled mark.
commands.tips: Useful for review comments and coordination notes.

commands.name: GETSEL
commands.description: Reports the number of objects in the current selection.
commands.example: Run after selecting objects.
commands.tips: Express tool for quick selection counts.

commands.name: GETVAR
commands.description: Reports the current value of a system variable.
commands.example: Enter variable name at prompt.
commands.tips: Quick way to inspect drawing settings.

commands.name: GIZMO
commands.description: Toggles 3D move, rotate, and scale gizmos.
commands.example: Enable or disable gizmo display.
commands.tips: Turn off when gizmos obscure small parts.

commands.name: GRADIENT
commands.description: Fills closed areas with a smooth color gradient.
commands.example: Select boundary and choose one-color or two-color gradient.
commands.tips: Presentation drawings often use subtle gradients for emphasis.

commands.name: GRID
commands.description: Displays a grid pattern in the drawing area.
commands.example: Toggle with F7 or the status bar.
commands.tips: Snap and Grid settings are independent.

commands.name: GROUP
commands.description: Creates a named selection group of objects that can be picked together.
commands.example: Create group name and select member objects.
commands.tips: Groups differ from blocks because each object remains editable separately.

commands.name: GROUPEDIT
commands.description: Adds or removes objects from a group.
commands.example: Select group and add or remove members.
commands.tips: Edit groups without exploding them.

commands.name: HATCH
commands.description: Fills an enclosed area or selected objects with a hatch pattern or gradient.
commands.example: Pick an internal point inside a closed boundary or select objects.
commands.tips: Use HATCHEDIT to modify an existing hatch pattern or scale.

commands.name: HATCHEDIT
commands.description: Modifies an existing hatch or fill pattern.
commands.example: Select hatch → adjust pattern, scale, angle, or boundary.
commands.tips: Use Recreate boundary when the hatch no longer matches enclosing geometry.

commands.name: HATCHGENERATEBOUNDARY
commands.description: Regenerates the boundary of an existing hatch.
commands.example: Select hatch object.
commands.tips: Use when hatch boundaries become invalid.

commands.name: HATCHSETORIGIN
commands.description: Sets hatch pattern origin for alignment.
commands.example: Select hatch and pick origin.
commands.tips: Align patterns across adjacent rooms.

commands.name: HATCHTOBACK
commands.description: Sends all hatch objects behind all other geometry.
commands.example: Run command; no selection required.
commands.tips: Prevents hatches from covering linework.

commands.name: HELIX
commands.description: Creates a 3D helical spline for springs, threads, and ramps.
commands.example: Define base center, base radius, top radius, and turn height.
commands.tips: Combine with SWEEP to model thread forms along a path.

commands.name: HELP
commands.description: Opens the help system for command and feature documentation.
commands.example: Type HELP or press F1.
commands.tips: Search help while learning unfamiliar commands.

commands.name: HIDE
commands.description: Regenerates a 3D model view with hidden lines suppressed.
commands.example: Run HIDE in a 3D wireframe or parallel view.
commands.tips: Visual styles now handle most hidden-line display needs.

commands.name: HIDEOBJECTS
commands.description: Temporarily hides selected objects from view.
commands.example: Select objects to hide.
commands.tips: Use SHOWALL or ISOLATEOBJECTS End to reveal them.

commands.name: HYPERLINK
commands.description: Attaches a hyperlink to an object or inserts hyperlink text.
commands.example: Select object and enter URL or file path.
commands.tips: Link title block cells to project folders or specs.

commands.name: ID
commands.description: Displays the UCS coordinate values of a specified point.
commands.example: Pick a point to read X, Y, Z coordinates.
commands.tips: Useful for verifying insertion points and survey data.

commands.name: IMAGEADJUST
commands.description: Adjusts brightness, contrast, and fade of attached images.
commands.example: Select image and modify display settings.
commands.tips: Fade images so linework traces remain visible.

commands.name: IMAGEATTACH
commands.description: Attaches a raster image reference to the drawing.
commands.example: Choose image file, insertion point, scale, and rotation.
commands.tips: Use IMAGEADJUST for brightness, contrast, and fade.

commands.name: IMAGECLIP
commands.description: Clips the display of an attached image to a boundary.
commands.example: Select image and define rectangular or polygonal clip.
commands.tips: Clip oversized site photos to the plan area only.

commands.name: IMPORT
commands.description: Imports files from other formats into the current drawing.
commands.example: Select file type and placement options.
commands.tips: Verify units after importing STEP, IGES, or PDF geometry.

commands.name: IMPRINT
commands.description: Imprints edges onto a solid or surface where objects intersect.
commands.example: Select target solid and imprinting object.
commands.tips: Prepares faces for splitting or applying different materials.

commands.name: INSERT
commands.description: Inserts a block or drawing into the current drawing.
commands.example: Choose block name → insertion point → scale → rotation.
commands.tips: Use Design Center or Content Browser for standard parts.

commands.name: INTERFERE
commands.description: Creates temporary solids showing where 3D objects overlap.
commands.example: Select first set of solids, then second set.
commands.tips: Use during coordination checks to find clashes quickly.

commands.name: INTERSECT
commands.description: Creates a solid from the common volume of selected solids.
commands.example: Select overlapping solids.
commands.tips: Useful for complex mold and casting geometry.

commands.name: ISOLATEOBJECTS
commands.description: Hides all objects except those selected.
commands.example: Select objects to keep visible.
commands.tips: Use UNISOLATEOBJECTS to restore full visibility.

commands.name: ISOLINES
commands.description: Sets the number of isolines displayed on curved 3D surfaces.
commands.example: Enter number of isolines per surface.
commands.tips: More isolines improve visual readability of 3D forms.

commands.name: JOIN
commands.description: Joins similar objects into a single object.
commands.example: Select collinear lines, arcs, or polylines to join.
commands.tips: Use PEDIT Join for polylines that don't meet exactly.

commands.name: JUSTIFYTEXT
commands.description: Changes justification of text without moving the insertion point.
commands.example: Select text and pick new justification.
commands.tips: Use before aligning notes in title blocks.

commands.name: LAYCUR
commands.description: Changes the layer of selected objects to the current layer.
commands.example: Select objects to move to current layer.
commands.tips: Fast cleanup when objects were drawn on wrong layers.

commands.name: LAYDEL
commands.description: Deletes a layer and moves its objects to a specified layer.
commands.example: Select layer to delete and confirm object reassignment.
commands.tips: Cannot delete layer 0 or current layer.

commands.name: LAYER
commands.description: Manages layers and layer properties in the drawing.
commands.example: Opens Layer Properties Manager to create, freeze, lock, or change layers.
commands.tips: Use LAYISO to isolate the layer of selected objects.

commands.name: LAYERF
commands.description: Freezes layers of selected objects quickly.
commands.example: Select object on layer to freeze.
commands.tips: Express tool similar to LAYFRZ.

commands.name: LAYERP
commands.description: Restores the previous layer state after layer changes.
commands.example: Toggle layers, then run LAYERP to revert the last state.
commands.tips: Enable LAYERPMODE to track more layer history.

commands.name: LAYFRZ
commands.description: Freezes the layer of selected objects in all viewports.
commands.example: Select an object on the layer to freeze.
commands.tips: Frozen layers don't regenerate, improving performance.

commands.name: LAYISO
commands.description: Isolates layers of selected objects by turning off or locking others.
commands.example: Select objects on layers to isolate.
commands.tips: Use LAYUNISO to restore previous layer states.

commands.name: LAYMCH
commands.description: Changes the layer of selected objects to match a destination object.
commands.example: Select objects to change → select destination layer object.
commands.tips: Useful for cleaning up drawings imported from other sources.

commands.name: LAYMCUR
commands.description: Sets the current layer to match the layer of a selected object.
commands.example: Select object whose layer should become current.
commands.tips: Match layer before drawing new geometry.

commands.name: LAYMRG
commands.description: Merges selected layers into a target layer and removes the source layers.
commands.example: Select layers to merge, then choose destination layer.
commands.tips: Audit layer names before merging imported consultant files.

commands.name: LAYOFF
commands.description: Turns off the layer of selected objects.
commands.example: Select an object on the layer to turn off.
commands.tips: LAYON restores all turned-off layers.

commands.name: LAYON
commands.description: Turns on all layers that are currently turned off.
commands.example: Run LAYON to restore visibility across the drawing.
commands.tips: Use LAYUNISO if you only need to undo an isolate operation.

commands.name: LAYOUT
commands.description: Creates and modifies layout tabs for plotting.
commands.example: Create new layout or rename existing tabs.
commands.tips: Sheets for title blocks and viewports live here.

commands.name: LAYOUTCREATE
commands.description: Creates a new layout tab from a template.
commands.example: Choose template and layout name.
commands.tips: Standardize new sheets across projects.

commands.name: LAYPICK
commands.description: Sets current layer by picking an object on that layer.
commands.example: Pick any object to match its layer.
commands.tips: Express tool similar to LAYMCUR.

commands.name: LAYSTD
commands.description: Manages layer standards and translation mappings.
commands.example: Define or apply layer standard rules.
commands.tips: Pair with CHECKSTANDARDS for compliance.

commands.name: LAYTHW
commands.description: Thaws all frozen layers in the current viewport.
commands.example: Run LAYTHW to restore frozen layers to a visible state.
commands.tips: Use VPLAYER for viewport-specific freeze control in layouts.

commands.name: LAYTRANS
commands.description: Translates foreign layers to local standards.
commands.example: Load translation map and apply.
commands.tips: Essential for imported consultant files.

commands.name: LAYUNISO
commands.description: Restores layer visibility and status before the last LAYISO command.
commands.example: Run after finishing work in an isolated layer state.
commands.tips: Pair LAYISO and LAYUNISO during detail checks on complex plans.

commands.name: LAYVPI
commands.description: Controls viewport-specific layer overrides.
commands.example: Select viewport and override properties.
commands.tips: Different display per viewport if needed.

commands.name: LAYWALK
commands.description: Dynamically isolates layers as you select them in a dialog.
commands.example: Pick layers in the list to inspect one at a time.
commands.tips: Exit restores prior visibility automatically.

commands.name: LEADER
commands.description: Creates a line with an arrow and annotation.
commands.example: Arrow location → leader points → annotation text.
commands.tips: Use MLEADER for multileader styles with blocks or text.

commands.name: LEADEREDIT
commands.description: Edits legacy leader text and vertices.
commands.example: Select leader and modify content.
commands.tips: For older leader objects.

commands.name: LENGTHEN
commands.description: Changes the length of lines and arcs without affecting direction or radius.
commands.example: Choose Delta, Percent, Total, or Dynamic, then select an object.
commands.tips: Dynamic mode lets you drag an endpoint to a new location interactively.

commands.name: LIGHT
commands.description: Creates point, spot, and web lights for rendering.
commands.example: Choose light type, location, and intensity properties.
commands.tips: Use sun and sky settings for exterior architectural renders.

commands.name: LIGHTLIST
commands.description: Lists and edits lights in the drawing.
commands.example: Adjust intensity in the light palette.
commands.tips: Disable unused lights to speed rendering.

commands.name: LIMITS
commands.description: Sets an invisible drawing boundary in model space.
commands.example: Lower left corner → upper right corner.
commands.tips: Less common in modern workflows but still on certification exams.

commands.name: LINE
commands.description: Creates straight line segments between specified points.
commands.example: Specify first point, then next points. Press Enter or Esc to finish.
commands.tips: Use Ortho mode (F8) for horizontal and vertical lines. Type C to close a polygon.

commands.name: LINETYPE
commands.description: Loads, creates, and assigns linetypes.
commands.example: Open linetype manager, load desired LIN file definitions.
commands.tips: Keep custom linetypes in a shared library folder for teams.

commands.name: LINEWEIGHT
commands.description: Sets default lineweight and controls lineweight display.
commands.example: Choose default lineweight and toggle display.
commands.tips: Plot with object lineweights or by color depending on office standards.

commands.name: LIST
commands.description: Displays property data for selected objects.
commands.example: Select objects → review text window output.
commands.tips: Copy list output to the clipboard for documentation.

commands.name: LIVESECTION
commands.description: Toggles live section display for section plane objects.
commands.example: Select section plane and enable live section.
commands.tips: Inspect interior geometry without cutting the model permanently.

commands.name: LOFT
commands.description: Creates a solid or surface between cross sections.
commands.example: Select cross sections in order → Enter.
commands.tips: Add guide curves for complex transitions.

commands.name: LOGFILEOFF
commands.description: Stops logging command text to a file.
commands.example: Run to close active log session.
commands.tips: Pair with LOGFILEON for session logs.

commands.name: LOGFILEON
commands.description: Starts logging command text to a file.
commands.example: Specify log file path.
commands.tips: Use LOGFILEOFF to stop logging.

commands.name: LTSCALE
commands.description: Sets the global linetype scale factor for the drawing.
commands.example: Enter a scale value such as 1 for model space or viewport-specific values.
commands.tips: If linetypes look solid, check LTSCALE and PSLTSCALE together.

commands.name: MAPIMPORT
commands.description: Imports map data from GIS sources into the drawing.
commands.example: Select file format and coordinate system.
commands.tips: Verify units and projection before tracing.

commands.name: MARKUP
commands.description: Creates review markup in the drawing.
commands.example: Add markup geometry and comments.
commands.tips: Use with markup manager for team review.

commands.name: MARKUPMANAGER
commands.description: Manages drawing markup and review comments.
commands.example: Browse and navigate markup entries.
commands.tips: Track review cycles on shared projects.

commands.name: MASSPROP
commands.description: Calculates mass properties of regions or solids.
commands.example: Select regions or 3D solids.
commands.tips: Export results to a file for reports.

commands.name: MATCHPROP
commands.description: Applies the properties of a source object to other objects.
commands.example: Select source object → select destination objects.
commands.tips: Use Settings to choose which properties to match.

commands.name: MATERIALS
commands.description: Assigns and edits render materials on 3D objects.
commands.example: Browse library, assign material, adjust scale and mapping.
commands.tips: Keep material libraries organized by project type.

commands.name: MEASURE
commands.description: Places point objects or blocks at measured intervals along an object.
commands.example: Select object → segment length.
commands.tips: Great for fence posts, lighting layouts, and stationing.

commands.name: MEASUREGEOM
commands.description: Measures distance, radius, angle, area, and volume from the ribbon.
commands.example: Choose Quick, Distance, Radius, Angle, Area, or Volume.
commands.tips: Quick mode shows cumulative distance along a path.

commands.name: MENUBAR
commands.description: Displays or hides the menu bar above the ribbon.
commands.example: Set to 1 to show, 0 to hide.
commands.tips: Some users prefer classic menu access.

commands.name: MENULOAD
commands.description: Loads or unloads partial menu files.
commands.example: Select MNU or CUI partial menu.
commands.tips: Customize interface with partial menus.

commands.name: MESH
commands.description: Creates mesh objects with editable faces, edges, and vertices.
commands.example: Select primitive type or convert existing geometry to mesh.
commands.tips: Mesh modeling is useful for organic forms and smoothing.

commands.name: MESHCAP
commands.description: Closes open edges of a mesh with a cover face.
commands.example: Select open mesh edges to cap.
commands.tips: Creates watertight meshes for printing.

commands.name: MESHCOLLAPSE
commands.description: Collapses mesh faces or edges to simplify geometry.
commands.example: Select mesh subobjects to collapse.
commands.tips: Reduce complexity before export.

commands.name: MESHCREASE
commands.description: Applies crease edges to control mesh smoothing.
commands.example: Select mesh edges and crease level.
commands.tips: Sharpen edges on smoothed meshes.

commands.name: MESHEXPLODE
commands.description: Explodes mesh objects into faces.
commands.example: Select mesh and explode level.
commands.tips: Edit individual faces afterward.

commands.name: MESHEXTRUDE
commands.description: Extrudes mesh faces to add depth.
commands.example: Select mesh faces and extrusion height.
commands.tips: Useful for adding thickness to mesh panels.

commands.name: MESHMERGE
commands.description: Merges adjacent mesh faces.
commands.example: Select mesh faces to combine.
commands.tips: Simplify mesh before export.

commands.name: MESHPRIMITIVE
commands.description: Creates basic mesh primitives such as boxes, spheres, and cylinders.
commands.example: Choose primitive type and dimensions.
commands.tips: Starting point for mesh-based conceptual models.

commands.name: MESHREFINE
commands.description: Subdivides mesh faces to add detail.
commands.example: Select mesh objects to refine.
commands.tips: Refine locally before smoothing organic shapes.

commands.name: MESHSMOOTH
commands.description: Smooths mesh objects by increasing face count.
commands.example: Select mesh and choose smooth level.
commands.tips: Higher levels increase file size and regen time.

commands.name: MESHSPIN
commands.description: Revolves mesh geometry around an axis.
commands.example: Select mesh profile and axis.
commands.tips: Creates revolved mesh forms.

commands.name: MESHUNCREASE
commands.description: Removes crease settings from mesh edges.
commands.example: Select creased edges to smooth.
commands.tips: Restore smooth transitions on mesh edges.

commands.name: MINSERT
commands.description: Inserts a rectangular array of block references in one step.
commands.example: Select block, rows, columns, and spacing.
commands.tips: Older workflow; ARRAY is more flexible for modern drafting.

commands.name: MIRROR
commands.description: Creates a mirrored copy of objects across a mirror line.
commands.example: Select objects → first point of mirror line → second point.
commands.tips: Erase source objects? No keeps the original; Yes replaces with the mirror.

commands.name: MIRRTEXT
commands.description: Controls whether text is mirrored with the MIRROR command.
commands.example: Set to 0 to keep text readable after mirror.
commands.tips: Set 0 for standard readable annotations.

commands.name: MLEADER
commands.description: Creates multileader objects with text, blocks, or tolerance.
commands.example: Arrowhead location → landing location → enter text.
commands.tips: Define styles in MLEADERSTYLE for consistent callouts.

commands.name: MLEADERALIGN
commands.description: Aligns and spaces selected multileaders.
commands.example: Select multileaders and choose alignment reference.
commands.tips: Clean up crowded annotation on details and sections.

commands.name: MLEADERCOLLECT
commands.description: Combines multiple multileaders into a single stacked callout.
commands.example: Select multileaders to merge under one arrow.
commands.tips: Useful for tagging repeated fasteners or notes.

commands.name: MLEADEREDIT
commands.description: Edits multileader content, landing, and arrow placement.
commands.example: Select a multileader and modify text or block content.
commands.tips: Use MLEADERALIGN to line up multiple callouts.

commands.name: MLEADERSTYLE
commands.description: Controls arrow, landing, and content settings for multileaders.
commands.example: Define leader format, text attachment, and block content.
commands.tips: Standardize callout styles early for consistent construction documents.

commands.name: MLEDIT
commands.description: Edits multiline vertices, cuts, and joins.
commands.example: Select multiline and choose edit option from the dialog.
commands.tips: Adjust wall intersections in plan drawings.

commands.name: MLINE
commands.description: Creates multiline parallel strokes defined by a multiline style.
commands.example: Pick points to draw parallel wall lines or double-line paths.
commands.tips: Define wall thickness in MLSTYLE before starting plans.

commands.name: MLSTYLE
commands.description: Creates and edits multiline styles with parallel offsets.
commands.example: Add elements, set offsets, color, and linetype for each stroke.
commands.tips: Save office-standard wall styles for consistent plan graphics.

commands.name: MOCORO
commands.description: Moves and copies objects in one combined operation.
commands.example: Select objects and define move/copy options.
commands.tips: Express tool time-saver for layout work.

commands.name: MOVE
commands.description: Moves selected objects a specified distance in a specified direction.
commands.example: Select objects → base point → second point.
commands.tips: Use @distance<angle for polar coordinates, e.g. @10<45.

commands.name: MOVECOPY
commands.description: Moves selected objects and optionally copies them.
commands.example: Select objects and displacement.
commands.tips: Express tool combining move workflows.

commands.name: MOVEFACE
commands.description: Moves a face on a 3D solid.
commands.example: Select face and displacement.
commands.tips: Direct solid editing without booleans.

commands.name: MREDO
commands.description: Redoes multiple UNDO operations.
commands.example: Run after several UNDO commands.
commands.tips: Restores a batch of undone steps.

commands.name: MSLICE
commands.description: Slices a solid using a plane and optionally keeps both halves.
commands.example: Select solid and define slicing plane.
commands.tips: Similar to SLICE with multi-body options.

commands.name: MSPACE
commands.description: Switches from paper space to model space in a layout viewport.
commands.example: Double-click viewport or type MSPACE.
commands.tips: Use PSPACE to return to layout editing.

commands.name: MTEDIT
commands.description: Edits multiline text in a dedicated editor.
commands.example: Select mtext object to open editor.
commands.tips: Double-click mtext for the same result.

commands.name: MTEXT
commands.description: Creates multiline text with formatting options.
commands.example: Specify text boundary → enter content in the editor.
commands.tips: Use columns and background mask for notes and title blocks.

commands.name: MULTIPLE
commands.description: Repeats the next command until canceled.
commands.example: Type MULTIPLE then the command name.
commands.tips: Avoids retyping repetitive commands.

commands.name: MVIEW
commands.description: Creates and controls layout viewports.
commands.example: Specify viewport bounds on a layout tab.
commands.tips: Use MVSETUP for standardized viewport and title block creation.

commands.name: MVSETUP
commands.description: Sets up viewports and title blocks for layout sheets.
commands.example: Choose units and sheet layout template options.
commands.tips: Automates common sheet creation for beginners.

commands.name: NAVBAR
commands.description: Shows or hides the navigation bar.
commands.example: Toggle bar display in viewport.
commands.tips: Quick access to orbit and walk tools.

commands.name: NAVSWHEEL
commands.description: Displays a steering wheel for quick pan, zoom, and orbit navigation.
commands.example: Open steering wheel and drag wedges for navigation.
commands.tips: Helpful for new users exploring complex 3D models.

commands.name: NCOPY
commands.description: Copies nested objects from within blocks or xrefs.
commands.example: Select nested object and specify base and destination points.
commands.tips: Extract linework from xrefs without binding the reference.

commands.name: NETLOAD
commands.description: Loads a .NET application assembly into the session.
commands.example: Browse to DLL file and load.
commands.tips: Only load trusted plugins from known developers.

commands.name: NEW
commands.description: Creates a new drawing from a template.
commands.example: Select template file and confirm units and title block setup.
commands.tips: Maintain company templates for consistent layers and styles.

commands.name: NEWSHEETSET
commands.description: Creates a new sheet set for organized publishing.
commands.example: Follow wizard to define sheet set.
commands.tips: Start of sheet set management workflow.

commands.name: OFFSET
commands.description: Creates parallel copies of lines, polylines, circles, or arcs at a set distance.
commands.example: Specify distance → select object → side to offset.
commands.tips: Use Through option to offset through a picked point.

commands.name: OFFSETEDGE
commands.description: Offsets an edge on a 3D solid.
commands.example: Select edge and offset distance.
commands.tips: Useful for edge-based solid modeling.

commands.name: OOPS
commands.description: Restores objects deleted by the last ERASE command.
commands.example: Run immediately after an accidental erase.
commands.tips: Only works for the most recent erase operation.

commands.name: OPEN
commands.description: Opens an existing drawing file.
commands.example: Browse to DWG or DXF file.
commands.tips: Use RECENT tab for fast access to recent projects.

commands.name: OPENSHEETSET
commands.description: Opens an existing sheet set for editing.
commands.example: Browse to DST file and open.
commands.tips: Access previously configured sheet sets.

commands.name: OPTIONS
commands.description: Opens application and drawing settings such as paths, display, and selection.
commands.example: Review Files, Display, Selection, and Drafting tabs.
commands.tips: Set autosave interval and support paths before large projects.

commands.name: ORTHO
commands.description: Constrains cursor movement to horizontal and vertical directions.
commands.example: Toggle with F8.
commands.tips: Temporarily override with Shift while drawing.

commands.name: OSNAP
commands.description: Sets running object snaps for precise point selection.
commands.example: Enable Endpoint, Midpoint, Center, Intersection as needed.
commands.tips: F3 toggles object snap on and off.

commands.name: OSNAP3D
commands.description: Sets running 3D object snaps.
commands.example: Enable vertex, edge, and face snaps.
commands.tips: Essential for accurate 3D modeling picks.

commands.name: OVERKILL
commands.description: Removes duplicate or overlapping geometry.
commands.example: Select objects → confirm tolerance settings.
commands.tips: Excellent for cleaning imported or messy drawings.

commands.name: PAGESETUP
commands.description: Controls layout page settings for plotting and publishing.
commands.example: Define printer, sheet size, plot scale, and plot area.
commands.tips: Name setups by sheet type for repeatable publishing.

commands.name: PAN
commands.description: Shifts the view without changing magnification.
commands.example: Hold and drag to reposition the drawing.
commands.tips: Hold the mouse wheel and drag for real-time panning.

commands.name: PARTIALOPEN
commands.description: Opens only selected layers from a large file.
commands.example: Choose layers to load.
commands.tips: Improves performance on huge drawings.

commands.name: PASTEBLOCK
commands.description: Pastes clipboard contents as a new block at the selected insertion point.
commands.example: Specify insertion point for pasted block.
commands.tips: Useful when transferring reusable details between projects.

commands.name: PASTECLIP
commands.description: Pastes objects from the clipboard into the drawing.
commands.example: Run PASTECLIP and place the clipboard contents.
commands.tips: Paste into another drawing to transfer geometry between projects.

commands.name: PASTEORIG
commands.description: Pastes clipboard objects using their original coordinates.
commands.example: Copy in one drawing, switch files, run PASTEORIG.
commands.tips: Ideal for coordinating multi-file project assemblies.

commands.name: PASTESPEC
commands.description: Pastes clipboard data with format options.
commands.example: Choose paste type and insertion point.
commands.tips: Control embedded Excel or image data.

commands.name: PDFATTACH
commands.description: Attaches a PDF file as an underlay reference.
commands.example: Select PDF, page, insertion point, scale, and rotation.
commands.tips: Snap to PDF geometry when vector data is available.

commands.name: PDFCLIP
commands.description: Clips the visible area of an attached PDF underlay.
commands.example: Select PDF underlay and define clip boundary.
commands.tips: Reduce clutter when only one sheet area is needed.

commands.name: PDFIMPORT
commands.description: Imports geometry, solids, text, and images from a PDF file.
commands.example: Select PDF, choose import type and insertion point.
commands.tips: Vector PDFs import more cleanly than scanned pages.

commands.name: PEDIT
commands.description: Edits polylines and converts lines and arcs into polylines.
commands.example: Select polyline → choose Join, Width, Spline, or Edit vertex.
commands.tips: Use Join to combine multiple segments into one polyline.

commands.name: PFACE
commands.description: Creates a 3D mesh face defined by vertex points.
commands.example: Enter vertex numbers for each face corner.
commands.tips: Older mesh face creation method.

commands.name: PICKADD
commands.description: Controls whether subsequent selections add to the set.
commands.example: Set to 2 for additive selection behavior.
commands.tips: Affects shift-select behavior.

commands.name: PICKAUTO
commands.description: Controls automatic selection at blank pick points.
commands.example: Set to 1 to enable auto window selection.
commands.tips: Adjust if accidental selections occur.

commands.name: PICKFIRST
commands.description: Controls whether objects must be selected before commands.
commands.example: Set to 1 for select-first workflow.
commands.tips: Most users prefer pick-first enabled.

commands.name: PICKSTYLE
commands.description: Controls group and hatch associative selection behavior.
commands.example: Set bitcode for group and hatch selection.
commands.tips: Adjust if hatches select with boundaries.

commands.name: PLAN
commands.description: Sets the viewing direction parallel to a user coordinate system.
commands.example: Current UCS, World, or named UCS.
commands.tips: PLAN W is a quick way to return to top view.

commands.name: PLANESURF
commands.description: Creates a planar surface from objects or corner points.
commands.example: Pick objects or define rectangular plane corners.
commands.tips: Quick way to cap openings before solid modeling.

commands.name: PLOT
commands.description: Plots or prints a drawing to a device or file.
commands.example: Select printer/plotter → paper size → scale → plot area.
commands.tips: Save PAGESETUP for repeatable title block layouts.

commands.name: PLOTSTAMP
commands.description: Adds a configurable stamp to plotted output.
commands.example: Enable stamp and define fields such as date and file name.
commands.tips: Use for submittal tracking on printed sets.

commands.name: PNGOUT
commands.description: Exports the current view to a PNG image file.
commands.example: Select area or current view and file name.
commands.tips: Quick way to share previews with non-CAD users.

commands.name: POINT
commands.description: Creates a point object at a specified location.
commands.example: Specify point location.
commands.tips: Change point display style with PTYPE.

commands.name: POINTCLOUDATTACH
commands.description: Attaches a point cloud scan for reference modeling.
commands.example: Select scan file and define insertion.
commands.tips: Use index files for faster performance on large scans.

commands.name: POINTCLOUDMANAGER
commands.description: Manages point cloud display and clipping.
commands.example: Adjust density and region settings.
commands.tips: Lower density improves navigation speed.

commands.name: POLYGON
commands.description: Creates an equilateral closed polyline.
commands.example: Number of sides → center → Inscribed or Circumscribed → radius.
commands.tips: Useful for hex bolts, nuts, and regular shapes.

commands.name: POLYLINE
commands.description: Creates a single object composed of connected line and arc segments.
commands.example: Start point → successive vertices → Enter to finish.
commands.tips: Use PEDIT to join lines into a polyline or add width and bulge values.

commands.name: POLYSOLID
commands.description: Creates a 3D wall-like solid by extruding a profile along a path.
commands.example: Set height and width, then pick path points.
commands.tips: Fast method for conceptual architectural mass walls.

commands.name: PRESSPULL
commands.description: Extrudes or offsets bounded areas into 3D solids or surfaces.
commands.example: Click inside a closed area and specify distance.
commands.tips: Works on regions and closed boundaries without a separate EXTRUDE step.

commands.name: PREVIEW
commands.description: Previews the drawing as it will plot.
commands.example: Run before sending sheets to plot.
commands.tips: Catch scale and orientation mistakes early.

commands.name: PROPERTIES
commands.description: Controls properties of existing objects via the Properties palette.
commands.example: Select objects and edit layer, color, linetype, and more.
commands.tips: Ctrl+1 toggles the Properties palette quickly.

commands.name: PSETUPIN
commands.description: Imports page setup into the current layout.
commands.example: Select source drawing and page setup name.
commands.tips: Reuse plot settings from other files.

commands.name: PSLTSCALE
commands.description: Controls whether linetypes appear the same width in paper space viewports.
commands.example: Set to 1 for viewport-adjusted linetype scaling.
commands.tips: Set MSLTSCALE similarly in model space for consistent behavior.

commands.name: PSPACE
commands.description: Switches from model space to paper space on a layout tab.
commands.example: Double-click outside viewport or type PSPACE.
commands.tips: Edit title blocks and sheet notes in paper space.

commands.name: PTYPE
commands.description: Sets the display style and size for point objects.
commands.example: Choose point style and size in dialog.
commands.tips: Make points visible when using DIVIDE or survey data.

commands.name: PUBLISH
commands.description: Publishes sheets or drawings to plotter, PDF, or DWF.
commands.example: Add sheets to publish list and start batch output.
commands.tips: Save sheet lists for recurring submittal packages.

commands.name: PUBLISHOPTIONS
commands.description: Sets default batch publish options.
commands.example: Configure output folder and naming.
commands.tips: Save time on recurring publish jobs.

commands.name: PURGE
commands.description: Removes unused named objects such as layers, blocks, and linetypes.
commands.example: Select categories → choose items → Purge.
commands.tips: Use -PURGE for command-line batch purging.

commands.name: PYRAMID
commands.description: Creates a 3D solid pyramid or frustum with polygonal base.
commands.example: Specify sides, base, and height or apex.
commands.tips: Set sides to 4 for rectangular pyramid forms.

commands.name: QBLOCK
commands.description: Quickly creates a block from selected objects.
commands.example: Select objects and enter a block name.
commands.tips: Faster than the full BLOCK dialog for simple cases.

commands.name: QDIM
commands.description: Creates a series of dimensions quickly.
commands.example: Select objects → specify dimension line location.
commands.tips: Fast for evenly spaced linear dimensions.

commands.name: QLEADER
commands.description: Creates quick leaders with text or block content.
commands.example: Arrow location → leader vertices → annotation.
commands.tips: Switch to MLEADER for style-controlled multileaders.

commands.name: QNEW
commands.description: Starts a new drawing using the configured default template.
commands.example: Run QNEW to bypass the template selection dialog.
commands.tips: Set default template in OPTIONS for consistent startup.

commands.name: QSAVE
commands.description: Saves the current drawing without opening a dialog.
commands.example: Press Ctrl+S or run QSAVE.
commands.tips: First save prompts for a file name if the drawing is new.

commands.name: QSELECT
commands.description: Creates a selection set by filtering object properties.
commands.example: Apply to entire drawing or current selection, then filter by layer or type.
commands.tips: Combine with LAYMCH to bulk-move objects to the correct layer.

commands.name: QUICKCALC
commands.description: Opens a calculator palette for numeric input while drafting.
commands.example: Perform arithmetic and paste results directly to the command line.
commands.tips: Use history and unit conversion tools for field measurements.

commands.name: QUIT
commands.description: Closes the application after prompting to save open drawings.
commands.example: Type QUIT or EXIT.
commands.tips: Use CLOSEALL first if you only want to close drawings.

commands.name: QVLAYOUT
commands.description: Creates a quick layout with a viewport.
commands.example: Choose template and viewport scale.
commands.tips: Rapid single-sheet setup.

commands.name: RAY
commands.description: Creates a semi-infinite construction line from a start point.
