commands.example: Start point → through point.
commands.tips: Useful for layout and alignment references.

commands.name: REALTIME
commands.description: Starts realtime zoom and pan navigation.
commands.example: Right-click to switch zoom or pan mode.
commands.tips: Superseded by mouse wheel navigation.

commands.name: RECOVER
commands.description: Repairs a damaged drawing file.
commands.example: Select drawing file to recover.
commands.tips: Also try RECOVERALL for xrefs and nested references.

commands.name: RECOVERALL
commands.description: Repairs the current drawing and attached external references.
commands.example: Run RECOVERALL and confirm repair actions when prompted.
commands.tips: Try this before sending corrupted project files to support.

commands.name: RECTANGLE
commands.description: Creates a rectangular polyline from two opposite corner points.
commands.example: First corner → opposite corner.
commands.tips: Use @width,height for exact dimensions from the first corner.

commands.name: REDEFINE
commands.description: Restores a built-in command that was undefined.
commands.example: Enter command name to restore.
commands.tips: Use after UNDEFINE blocked a command.

commands.name: REDO
commands.description: Reverses the effect of the last UNDO.
commands.example: Type REDO or use Ctrl+Y.
commands.tips: Only available immediately after an UNDO.

commands.name: REDRAW
commands.description: Refreshes the display in the current viewport without regenerating.
commands.example: Type REDRAW to clear transient graphics.
commands.tips: Use REGEN when geometry appears out of sync after edits.

commands.name: REDRAWALL
commands.description: Redraws all viewports in the drawing.
commands.example: Run REDRAWALL to refresh every open viewport.
commands.tips: Helpful after scripts or custom routines modify display lists.

commands.name: REFCLOSE
commands.description: Saves or discards changes made during in-place reference editing.
commands.example: Choose Save reference changes or discard.
commands.tips: Pair with REFEDIT for temporary xref or block edits.

commands.name: REFEDIT
commands.description: Edits geometry inside a block or xref reference in place.
commands.example: Select reference, choose objects to edit, make changes, then REFCLOSE.
commands.tips: Prefer BEDIT for permanent block definition changes.

commands.name: REFSET
commands.description: Adds or removes objects from a working set during reference editing.
commands.example: Choose Add or Remove, then select objects.
commands.tips: Controls which geometry is editable inside REFEDIT.

commands.name: REGEN
commands.description: Regenerates the drawing from the current viewport.
commands.example: Type REGEN or RE.
commands.tips: Use REGENALL to regenerate all viewports in layouts.

commands.name: REGEN3
commands.description: Regenerates drawing and rebuilds 3D display data.
commands.example: Run when 3D display looks wrong.
commands.tips: Heavier than standard REGEN.

commands.name: REGENALL
commands.description: Regenerates all viewports in the drawing.
commands.example: Type REGENALL.
commands.tips: Helpful after scaling or heavy edits in paper space.

commands.name: REGENAUTO
commands.description: Controls automatic regeneration of the drawing after certain commands.
commands.example: Set automatic regen on or off.
commands.tips: Turn off on large files to reduce wait time.

commands.name: REGION
commands.description: Converts closed loops into 2D region objects for analysis and modeling.
commands.example: Select closed polylines, circles, or ellipses to convert.
commands.tips: Boolean operations on regions can simplify complex outlines.

commands.name: REINIT
commands.description: Reinitializes digitizer, tablet, and input devices.
commands.example: Select devices to reinitialize.
commands.tips: Troubleshoot input device issues.

commands.name: RELOAD
commands.description: Reloads selected xrefs from their source files.
commands.example: Select xref to refresh with latest saved version.
commands.tips: Use when consultants update background drawings.

commands.name: RENAME
commands.description: Renames blocks, layers, linetypes, and other named objects.
commands.example: Choose object type, select old name, enter new name.
commands.tips: Use PURGE after renaming to remove unused old definitions.

commands.name: RENDER
commands.description: Creates a photorealistic or realistically shaded image of a 3D model.
commands.example: Set materials and lights → start render.
commands.tips: Use RENDERPRESETS for quality vs. speed tradeoffs.

commands.name: RENDERCROP
commands.description: Renders only a cropped region of the view.
commands.example: Define crop window and render.
commands.tips: Fast test renders of small areas.

commands.name: RENDERPRESET
commands.description: Manages stored render quality presets.
commands.example: Save draft or high-quality presets.
commands.tips: Draft presets iterate faster.

commands.name: REVCLOUD
commands.description: Creates a revision cloud to highlight markup areas.
commands.example: Start point → arc length → draw cloud boundary.
commands.tips: Use Rectangular or Polygon style for uniform clouds.

commands.name: REVERSE
commands.description: Reverses the direction of selected lines, polylines, or hatch boundaries.
commands.example: Select lines, polylines, or hatches to flip direction.
commands.tips: Polyline direction affects linetype generation and path-based tools.

commands.name: REVOLVE
commands.description: Creates a solid or surface by revolving a profile around an axis.
commands.example: Select profile → axis start → axis end → angle.
commands.tips: 360° revolve is common for shafts and pulleys.

commands.name: REVSURF
commands.description: Creates a surface by revolving a profile around an axis.
commands.example: Select axis object, then profile curve and angle.
commands.tips: Alternative to REVOLVE when a surface result is needed.

commands.name: ROTATE
commands.description: Rotates objects around a base point by a specified angle.
commands.example: Select objects → base point → rotation angle or reference.
commands.tips: Use Copy option to keep the original and create a rotated copy.

commands.name: ROTATE3D
commands.description: Rotates objects about a 3D axis.
commands.example: Select objects, axis, and angle.
commands.tips: Command-line alternative to 3DROTATE.

commands.name: RTEXT
commands.description: Creates remote text linked to an external text file.
commands.example: Point to TXT file and place text.
commands.tips: Update notes by editing the external file.

commands.name: RTPAN
commands.description: Pans the view interactively in real time.
commands.example: Drag to pan the drawing.
commands.tips: Mouse wheel drag pan is faster today.

commands.name: RTZOOM
commands.description: Zooms the view interactively in real time.
commands.example: Drag up or down to zoom dynamically.
commands.tips: Legacy realtime navigation command.

commands.name: RULESURF
commands.description: Creates a ruled surface between two curves.
commands.example: Select first curve → second curve.
commands.tips: Use for transitional surfaces between profile edges.

commands.name: SAVE
commands.description: Saves the current drawing.
commands.example: Ctrl+S or QSAVE for quick save.
commands.tips: Enable automatic save in Options for safety.

commands.name: SAVEAS
commands.description: Saves the drawing under a new file name or format.
commands.example: Choose folder, file name, and DWG/DXF version if needed.
commands.tips: Save down a version when sharing with users on older releases.

commands.name: SCALE
commands.description: Enlarges or reduces selected objects proportionally.
commands.example: Select objects → base point → scale factor or reference length.
commands.tips: A factor of 1 keeps size; 2 doubles; 0.5 halves.

commands.name: SCREENSHOT
commands.description: Captures the current viewport as an image file.
commands.example: Choose save location and image format.
commands.tips: Quick way to share on-screen views.

commands.name: SCRIPT
commands.description: Executes a sequence of commands from a script file.
commands.example: Select SCR file to run automated command batch.
commands.tips: Use for repetitive plotting or cleanup tasks.

commands.name: SECTION
commands.description: Creates a region or 3D object representing a cross section of solids.
commands.example: Select solids and define section plane.
commands.tips: Use for generating section profiles from 3D models.

commands.name: SECTIONPLANE
commands.description: Creates a section object used to cut through 3D models.
commands.example: Pick three points or choose orthographic orientation.
commands.tips: Enable live section to inspect interior details while modeling.

commands.name: SECURELOAD
commands.description: Controls whether executable files load from unsafe paths.
commands.example: Set security level for LISP and apps.
commands.tips: Keep enabled for safer customization.

commands.name: SECURITYOPTIONS
commands.description: Sets drawing password and encryption options.
commands.example: Define open and modify passwords.
commands.tips: Store passwords securely.

commands.name: SELECTSIMILAR
commands.description: Adds objects similar to the selected object to the current selection.
commands.example: Select one object, then run SELECTSIMILAR.
commands.tips: Configure matching criteria such as layer, color, or type.

commands.name: SETBYBLOCK
commands.description: Sets selected object properties to ByBlock.
commands.example: Select objects in blocks to inherit block property behavior.
commands.tips: Common when preparing geometry inside block definitions.

commands.name: SETBYLAYER
commands.description: Sets selected object properties to ByLayer.
commands.example: Select objects with overrides and apply ByLayer settings.
commands.tips: Run before publishing to enforce office standards.

commands.name: SETUV
commands.description: Adjusts material UV mapping on faces.
commands.example: Select faces and adjust mapping.
commands.tips: Fixes stretched render textures.

commands.name: SETVAR
commands.description: Sets the value of a system variable.
commands.example: Enter variable name and new value.
commands.tips: Many settings are controlled via system variables.

commands.name: SHADEMODE
commands.description: Controls shaded display mode for the current viewport.
commands.example: Choose 2D wireframe, hidden, flat shaded, or Gouraud options.
commands.tips: Visual Styles palette offers more modern display control.

commands.name: SHADEPLOT
commands.description: Plots using shaded viewport display.
commands.example: Enable shaded plot in page setup.
commands.tips: Presentation plots with materials.

commands.name: SHARE
commands.description: Shares the drawing through cloud collaboration.
commands.example: Choose share target and permissions.
commands.tips: Requires a signed-in cloud account.

commands.name: SHEETSET
commands.description: Manages sheet sets for organized publishing of layout sheets.
commands.example: Create sheet set, add subsets, and publish.
commands.tips: Standardize sheet numbering across large projects.

commands.name: SHELL
commands.description: Hollows a 3D solid by removing faces and assigning wall thickness.
commands.example: Select solid, remove faces to open, then set thickness.
commands.tips: Useful for containers, enclosures, and wall assemblies.

commands.name: SHOWALL
commands.description: Restores visibility of all hidden objects.
commands.example: Run after temporary hide or isolate workflows.
commands.tips: Does not change layer on/off states.

commands.name: SHOWMOTION
commands.description: Plays recorded view animations and walkthroughs.
commands.example: Select animation from the list.
commands.tips: Use for client presentation playback.

commands.name: SKETCH
commands.description: Creates a series of line segments by freehand dragging.
commands.example: Press to record segments; pick Record when finished.
commands.tips: Legacy freehand tool; splines are smoother for most uses.

commands.name: SLICE
commands.description: Slices a solid with a plane, leaving one or both sides.
commands.example: Select solid → define slicing plane → keep side.
commands.tips: Use Z-axis or 3 points to define the cutting plane.

commands.name: SNAP
commands.description: Restricts cursor movement to specified intervals.
commands.example: Toggle with F9 or set snap spacing.
commands.tips: Object snap (OSNAP) is usually more useful than grid snap.

commands.name: SNAPANG
commands.description: Sets rotation angle for snap and grid.
commands.example: Enter angle or pick two points.
commands.tips: Align grid to angled building geometry.

commands.name: SNAPBASE
commands.description: Relocates snap and grid origin.
commands.example: Pick new base point.
commands.tips: Use with SNAPANG for skewed grids.

commands.name: SOLDRAW
commands.description: Generates profile lines and hidden lines in layout viewports from 3D solids.
commands.example: Select viewport after running SOLVIEW.
commands.tips: Works with SOLVIEW-created viewport setups.

commands.name: SOLID
commands.description: Creates solid-filled triangles or quadrilaterals in 2D space.
commands.example: Pick three or four corner points in order.
commands.tips: Older command; filled hatches are more flexible for most workflows.

commands.name: SOLIDCHECK
commands.description: Validates 3D solids for geometry errors.
commands.example: Select solids to inspect.
commands.tips: Run before boolean operations on imports.

commands.name: SOLIDEDIT
commands.description: Edits faces, edges, and bodies of 3D solid objects.
commands.example: Select solid, choose face, edge, or body editing option.
commands.tips: Move, offset, or delete individual faces for direct modeling.

commands.name: SOLPROF
commands.description: Creates profile blocks from 3D solids in layout viewports.
commands.example: Select solids while in paper space viewport.
commands.tips: Generates 2D linework from 3D models.

commands.name: SOLVIEW
commands.description: Creates floating viewports with orthographic views of 3D solids.
commands.example: Follow prompts for top, front, and side viewport creation.
commands.tips: Legacy workflow; VIEWBASE is more modern for documentation.

commands.name: SPELL
commands.description: Checks spelling in text and multileader notes.
commands.example: Select text objects or check the entire drawing.
commands.tips: Add custom dictionaries for company names and industry terms.

commands.name: SPHERE
commands.description: Creates a 3D solid sphere from center and radius.
commands.example: Center point → radius or diameter.
commands.tips: Useful for quick massing studies and mechanical primitives.

commands.name: SPLINE
commands.description: Creates a smooth curve through or near specified points.
commands.example: Specify fit points → Enter to finish.
commands.tips: Convert splines to polylines with SPLINEDIT if needed for CNC.

commands.name: SPLINEDIT
commands.description: Edits spline fit points, control points, and precision.
commands.example: Select spline and choose move point, refine, or convert options.
commands.tips: Convert to polyline when exporting to CNC or GIS workflows.

commands.name: STANDARDS
commands.description: Associates the drawing with a CAD standards file.
commands.example: Attach DWS file and configure checks.
commands.tips: Centralize rules for multi-user teams.

commands.name: STATUS
commands.description: Displays drawing status such as limits, snap spacing, and current layer.
commands.example: Type STATUS and review the text window report.
commands.tips: Helpful when troubleshooting unexpected behavior in shared files.

commands.name: STLOUT
commands.description: Exports solid objects to STL format for 3D printing.
commands.example: Select solids and specify output file.
commands.tips: Verify watertight solids before printing.

commands.name: STRETCH
commands.description: Stretches objects crossed by a selection window.
commands.example: Crossing window select → base point → displacement point.
commands.tips: Only vertices inside the crossing window move.

commands.name: SUBTRACT
commands.description: Removes overlapping regions of solids from another solid.
commands.example: Select solids to keep → select solids to subtract.
commands.tips: Order of selection matters: main body first.

commands.name: SUPERHATCH
commands.description: Creates hatches using images, blocks, or xref patterns.
commands.example: Choose hatch type and boundary.
commands.tips: Express tool for custom pattern fills.

commands.name: SURFBLEND
commands.description: Creates a smooth blend surface between two surfaces.
commands.example: Select two surfaces and blend constraints.
commands.tips: Useful for filleted surface transitions.

commands.name: SURFEXTEND
commands.description: Extends a surface to meet another surface or edge.
commands.example: Select surface edge and extension distance.
commands.tips: Useful when surfaces stop short of required contact.

commands.name: SURFEXTRACT
commands.description: Extracts faces or regions from solids as separate surfaces.
commands.example: Select solid faces to extract.
commands.tips: Use before editing complex solid faces independently.

commands.name: SURFFILLET
commands.description: Creates a fillet surface between two existing surfaces.
commands.example: Select first surface, second surface, and radius.
commands.tips: Use for smooth transitions in surface modeling.

commands.name: SURFLOFT
commands.description: Creates a lofted surface through a set of cross-section curves.
commands.example: Select cross sections in order.
commands.tips: Add guide curves to control surface shape.

commands.name: SURFNETWORK
commands.description: Creates a surface from a network of crossing curves.
commands.example: Select U and V direction curves.
commands.tips: Requires well-defined curve networks.

commands.name: SURFOFFSET
commands.description: Offsets a surface by a specified distance.
commands.example: Select surface and offset distance.
commands.tips: Check normal direction for offset side.

commands.name: SURFPATCH
commands.description: Creates a surface that fills a boundary loop.
commands.example: Select boundary edges or curves.
commands.tips: Closes gaps in surface models.

commands.name: SURFREVOLVE
commands.description: Creates a revolved surface from a profile curve.
commands.example: Select profile and axis of revolution.
commands.tips: Partial revolutions create open surface shells.

commands.name: SURFSCULPT
commands.description: Combines intersecting surfaces into a sculptured solid.
commands.example: Select surfaces that enclose a volume.
commands.tips: Automates closing surface envelopes.

commands.name: SURFSWEEP
commands.description: Creates a surface by sweeping a profile along a path.
commands.example: Select profile curve and sweep path.
commands.tips: Alternative to SWEEP when a surface body is required.

commands.name: SURFTRIM
commands.description: Trims a surface using curves or other surfaces as cutters.
commands.example: Select surface to trim, then cutting objects.
commands.tips: Keep cutting geometry simple for reliable results.

commands.name: SURFUNTRIM
commands.description: Removes trimmed areas from surfaces.
commands.example: Select surface and regions to untrim.
commands.tips: Restore surface area after trimming.

commands.name: SWEEP
commands.description: Creates a solid or surface by sweeping a profile along a path.
commands.example: Select profile → select path.
commands.tips: Path can be open or closed; profile must stay valid along path.

commands.name: SYSVARMONITOR
commands.description: Alerts when monitored system variables change.
commands.example: Add variables such as LTSCALE.
commands.tips: Catch unexpected setting changes.

commands.name: SYSVDLG
commands.description: Opens a dialog to browse and edit system variables.
commands.example: Search variable name and change value.
commands.tips: Easier than memorizing variable names.

commands.name: TABLE
commands.description: Creates an empty table object for schedules and bills of materials.
commands.example: Insertion point → rows/columns → header and data.
commands.tips: Link tables to external data with data extraction.

commands.name: TABLEEDIT
commands.description: Edits table cells and structure.
commands.example: Select table and modify cells.
commands.tips: Double-click cells for in-place editing.

commands.name: TABLESTYLE
commands.description: Defines cell styles, borders, and text for table objects.
commands.example: Create or edit table styles before inserting schedules.
commands.tips: Match title block table appearance with a dedicated table style.

commands.name: TABSURF
commands.description: Creates a tabulated surface by extruding a profile along a path.
commands.example: Select direction vector, then profile curve.
commands.tips: Direction vector length affects surface orientation.

commands.name: TCOUNT
commands.description: Adds sequential numbers to selected text objects.
commands.example: Select text and define starting number and increment.
commands.tips: Speeds up numbering door tags or detail references.

commands.name: TEXT
commands.description: Creates single-line text objects.
commands.example: Start point → height → rotation → enter text → Enter twice to finish.
commands.tips: Use %%d for degree symbol, %%p for plus/minus, %%c for diameter.

commands.name: TEXTALIGN
commands.description: Aligns text objects to references.
commands.example: Select text and alignment target.
commands.tips: Neaten notes on crowded details.

commands.name: TEXTEDIT
commands.description: Edits single-line or multiline text in place.
commands.example: Select text object and modify content in the editor.
commands.tips: Double-click text on screen for the same workflow in many setups.

commands.name: TEXTFIT
commands.description: Shrinks or stretches text to fit between two points.
commands.example: Select text and define fit points.
commands.tips: Express tool for title block adjustments.

commands.name: TEXTMASK
commands.description: Masks text behind geometry using a wipeout.
commands.example: Select text to apply mask.
commands.tips: Improves readability over hatches.

commands.name: TEXTSCR
commands.description: Opens the text window for command history review.
commands.example: Toggle text window open or closed.
commands.tips: F2 also opens the text window.

commands.name: TEXTSTYLE
commands.description: Creates and modifies text styles for fonts, height, and width.
commands.example: Define style name, font file, height, and effects.
commands.tips: Set height to zero in the style so text height can vary per object.

commands.name: TEXTTOFRONT
commands.description: Brings all text and multileader objects in front of other geometry.
commands.example: Run to raise annotation above hatches and lines.
commands.tips: Use All, Text, or Leader options as needed.

commands.name: TFRAMES
commands.description: Controls frame display for text and mtext objects.
commands.example: Toggle frames on or off globally.
commands.tips: Express tool for text frame visibility.

commands.name: THICKEN
commands.description: Converts surfaces into solids by adding thickness.
commands.example: Select surface → specify thickness direction and value.
commands.tips: Check surface normal direction if thickness appears inverted.

commands.name: THICKNESS
commands.description: Sets default 3D thickness for new 2D objects.
commands.example: Enter thickness at command line.
commands.tips: Legacy setting for pseudo-3D linework.

commands.name: TILEMODE
commands.description: Switches between model space and the last used layout.
commands.example: Set to 1 for model space, 0 for layout space.
commands.tips: Quick toggle when moving between model and sheets.

commands.name: TIME
commands.description: Reports drawing creation and editing time statistics.
commands.example: Run TIME and review total editing time values.
commands.tips: Use RESET to clear accumulated timers when starting a new phase.

commands.name: TOLERANCE
commands.description: Creates geometric tolerance feature control frames.
commands.example: Open dialog → define symbol, tolerance, and datum references.
commands.tips: Match company standards with saved tolerance styles.

commands.name: TOOLBAR
commands.description: Displays or hides named toolbars.
commands.example: Enter toolbar name and show option.
commands.tips: Legacy UI; ribbon replaced most toolbars.

commands.name: TOOLPALETTES
commands.description: Opens tool palettes for blocks, hatches, commands, and macros.
commands.example: Drag tools into the drawing or customize palette content.
commands.tips: Create project-specific palettes for repeated details.

commands.name: TORIENT
commands.description: Aligns text objects to a specified angle or to an object.
commands.example: Select text and define new orientation.
commands.tips: Useful for readable labels on rotated plan views.

commands.name: TORUS
commands.description: Creates a donut-shaped 3D solid torus.
commands.example: Center → torus radius → tube radius.
commands.tips: Self-intersecting tube sizes produce unusual but valid forms.

commands.name: TRACE
commands.description: Creates wide lines by specifying four corner points.
commands.example: Pick four points to define a filled quadrilateral trace.
commands.tips: Largely replaced by polylines with width or solid fills.

commands.name: TRANSPARENCY
commands.description: Sets transparency for selected objects or the default for new objects.
commands.example: Enter transparency value or select ByLayer.
commands.tips: Use subtle transparency for reference geometry.

commands.name: TRIM
commands.description: Trims objects to meet the edges of cutting edges.
commands.example: Select cutting edges → select objects to trim.
commands.tips: Press Enter without selecting cutting edges to trim all eligible boundaries.

commands.name: TRIMTEXT
commands.description: Trims text objects to fit within a boundary.
commands.example: Select text and trimming edge.
commands.tips: Express tool for crowded details.

commands.name: TRUSTEDPATHS
commands.description: Defines folders trusted for loading custom files.
commands.example: Add office standard support folder paths.
commands.tips: Required for loading LISP from network drives.

commands.name: TSCALE
commands.description: Scales text without changing insertion point.
commands.example: Select text and scale factor.
commands.tips: Express tool for quick text resizing.

commands.name: TXT2MTXT
commands.description: Converts single-line text objects into one multiline text object.
commands.example: Select text objects in reading order.
commands.tips: Helpful when consolidating legacy annotations.

commands.name: TXTEXP
commands.description: Explodes text into individual polyline outlines.
commands.example: Select text objects to explode.
commands.tips: Express tool for CNC or laser workflows.

commands.name: UCS
commands.description: Manages user coordinate systems.
commands.example: Origin → X-axis point → Y-axis point.
commands.tips: Use UCS World to return to the default coordinate system.

commands.name: UCS WORLD
commands.description: Restores the World Coordinate System.
commands.example: Type UCS, then W for World.
commands.tips: Return to default coordinates after angled work.

commands.name: UCSDETECT
commands.description: Automatically aligns UCS to detected faces.
commands.example: Hover over a face to preview UCS alignment.
commands.tips: Speeds 3D sketching on angled faces.

commands.name: UNDEFINE
commands.description: Disables a command name in the session.
commands.example: Enter command to block.
commands.tips: Use REDEFINE to restore it.

commands.name: UNDERLAY
commands.description: Manages attached underlay references such as PDF and DWF.
commands.example: Attach, clip, or adjust underlay settings.
commands.tips: Central tool for PDF and DWF references.

commands.name: UNDO
commands.description: Reverses the effect of recent commands.
commands.example: Type U or use Ctrl+Z.
commands.tips: UNDO can step back through multiple operations.

commands.name: UNGROUP
commands.description: Removes grouping from selected grouped objects.
commands.example: Select grouped objects and run UNGROUP.
commands.tips: Objects remain but are no longer picked as a unit.

commands.name: UNION
commands.description: Combines selected 3D solids into one solid.
commands.example: Select solids to combine.
commands.tips: Use SUBTRACT and INTERSECT for Boolean operations.

commands.name: UNISOLATEOBJECTS
commands.description: Restores visibility of objects hidden by isolate commands.
commands.example: Run to end object isolation.
commands.tips: End Isolate from the status bar performs the same action.

commands.name: UNITS
commands.description: Controls coordinate and angle display formats and precision.
commands.example: Set length type, precision, insertion scale.
commands.tips: Match drawing units to your industry standard early.

commands.name: UPDATEFIELD
commands.description: Updates field text to reflect current drawing values.
commands.example: Select objects containing fields.
commands.tips: Use before plotting if fields appear outdated.

commands.name: VIEW
commands.description: Saves and restores named model views.
commands.example: New → define view name and boundaries.
commands.tips: Use views in sheet sets and viewport creation.

commands.name: VIEWBASE
commands.description: Creates a base view from 3D model geometry on a layout.
commands.example: Select 3D objects and place base view on sheet.
commands.tips: Starting point for automated drawing views from models.

commands.name: VIEWDETAIL
commands.description: Creates a detail view from an existing drawing view.
commands.example: Select parent view and detail boundary.
commands.tips: Use for enlarged details linked to plan or elevation views.

commands.name: VIEWGO
commands.description: Restores a named view instantly.
commands.example: Choose saved view from list.
commands.tips: Fast navigation between preset views.

commands.name: VIEWPROJ
commands.description: Projects geometry from one view to another.
commands.example: Select source view and projection target.
commands.tips: Used in automated drawing view workflows.

commands.name: VIEWRES
commands.description: Sets the display quality for curved objects in the current viewport.
commands.example: Choose fast or high-quality circle and arc display.
commands.tips: Higher quality slows pan and zoom on dense drawings.

commands.name: VIEWSECTION
commands.description: Creates a section view from existing drawing views.
commands.example: Select parent view and define section line.
commands.tips: Updates when the parent model view changes.

commands.name: VIEWUPDATE
commands.description: Updates drawing views after model changes.
commands.example: Select views to refresh from model.
commands.tips: Run after editing 3D source geometry.

commands.name: VISUALSTYLES
commands.description: Applies visual styles such as conceptual, realistic, or x-ray.
commands.example: Select a style from the visual styles manager.
commands.tips: Switch to 2D Wireframe when returning to flat drafting tasks.

commands.name: VLIDE
commands.description: Opens the Visual LISP integrated development environment.
commands.example: Launch editor to write or debug LISP code.
commands.tips: For advanced customization and automation.

commands.name: VLISP
commands.description: Starts Visual LISP and displays the console.
commands.example: Run to open LISP console window.
commands.tips: Entry point for interactive LISP development.

commands.name: VLLOAD
commands.description: Loads, unloads, or lists Visual LISP applications.
commands.example: Choose VLX or FAS file to load.
commands.tips: Used with custom LISP automation routines.

commands.name: VPLAYER
commands.description: Controls layer visibility by viewport in paper space.
commands.example: Freeze or thaw layers in selected viewports.
commands.tips: Essential for plan, elevation, and detail sheets from one model.

commands.name: VPORTS
commands.description: Creates multiple model space viewports.
commands.example: Choose configuration such as Two Vertical or Four Equal.
commands.tips: Maximize a viewport with double-click inside it.

commands.name: VTOPTIONS
commands.description: Sets view transition and pan/zoom animation options.
commands.example: Adjust smooth transition settings.
commands.tips: Disable if motion causes discomfort.

commands.name: WALKFLY
commands.description: Switches between walk and fly navigation modes.
commands.example: Toggle mode during 3D navigation.
commands.tips: Walk keeps eye height fixed.

commands.name: WBLOCK
commands.description: Writes selected objects to a new drawing file as a block.
commands.example: Define block name, base point, and objects.
commands.tips: Common workflow for creating reusable library parts.

commands.name: WEDGE
commands.description: Creates a 3D solid wedge with a rectangular base.
commands.example: First corner → opposite corner → height.
commands.tips: Helpful for chamfered blocks and simple mechanical cuts.

commands.name: WHIPARC
commands.description: Controls whether arcs appear smooth or segmented.
commands.example: Set to 1 for smooth arc display.
commands.tips: Turn off on slow hardware if needed.

commands.name: WHOHAS
commands.description: Shows who has a shared drawing open on the network.
commands.example: Select drawing file on a shared server path.
commands.tips: Use before trying to open files others may be editing.

commands.name: WIPEOUT
commands.description: Creates a mask area that hides objects behind it in display order.
commands.example: Specify boundary points to create a masking polygon.
commands.tips: Place text over complex hatches using a wipeout background.

commands.name: WMFBIN
commands.description: Imports a Windows metafile into the drawing.
commands.example: Select WMF file and insertion point.
commands.tips: Legacy vector import format.

commands.name: WMFIN
commands.description: Imports a Windows metafile into the drawing.
commands.example: Select file and insertion point.
commands.tips: Legacy vector import format.

commands.name: WMFOUT
commands.description: Exports selected objects to a Windows metafile.
commands.example: Select objects and output path.
commands.tips: Useful for inserting drawings into office documents.

commands.name: WORKSPACE
commands.description: Switches between saved workspace layouts.
commands.example: Choose drafting or 3D workspace.
commands.tips: Save workspace after arranging palettes.

commands.name: WSSAVE
commands.description: Saves current UI layout as a workspace.
commands.example: Enter workspace name.
commands.tips: Create discipline-specific layouts.

commands.name: WSSETTINGS
commands.description: Configures workspace behavior and save options.
commands.example: Adjust auto-save and switch settings.
commands.tips: Control how workspaces persist.

commands.name: XBIND
commands.description: Binds layers, linetypes, text styles, and blocks from xrefs into the host drawing.
commands.example: Select xref-dependent symbols to bind.
commands.tips: Differs from BIND which binds entire xref files.

commands.name: XCLIP
commands.description: Crops the display of a block or xref to a boundary.
commands.example: Select reference, choose polygonal or rectangular clip boundary.
commands.tips: XCLIPFRAME controls whether the clip boundary is visible.

commands.name: XCLIPFRAME
commands.description: Controls visibility of clip frame boundaries.
commands.example: Set frames on, off, or hidden.
commands.tips: Hide frames before final plots.

commands.name: XCOMPARE
commands.description: Compares attached xref files and shows revision differences.
commands.example: Open comparison palette and inspect xref changes.
commands.tips: Speeds coordination when consultants submit updated backgrounds.

commands.name: XLINE
commands.description: Creates an infinite construction line.
commands.example: Point on line → through point or angle.
commands.tips: Construction lines don't plot unless placed on a plotting layer.

commands.name: XLOADCTL
commands.description: Controls demand loading of xref references.
commands.example: Set value for load on open or demand.
commands.tips: Affects performance with many xrefs.

commands.name: XOPEN
commands.description: Opens an attached xref for editing in its own window.
commands.example: Select xref reference to open source drawing.
commands.tips: Save and reload xref to update the host drawing.

commands.name: XREF
commands.description: Manages external references attached to the current drawing.
commands.example: Attach DWG, image, PDF, or other reference files.
commands.tips: Bind or Overlay controls how xref changes affect the host drawing.

commands.name: XREFNOTIFY
commands.description: Controls notification when xrefs change on disk.
commands.example: Set to 2 to enable reload notifications.
commands.tips: Stay aware of consultant file updates.

commands.name: XREFSTATE
commands.description: Reports whether xrefs are loaded, unloaded, or not found.
commands.example: Run and review xref status report.
commands.tips: Diagnose broken reference paths quickly.

commands.name: XREPATH
commands.description: Changes the path of xref and image references.
commands.example: Select references and enter new path.
commands.tips: Fix broken xref paths after folder moves.

commands.name: ZOOM
commands.description: Increases or decreases the magnification of the drawing view.
commands.example: Z Enter E Enter for Extents, or Z Enter W for Window.
commands.tips: Double-click the mouse wheel for Zoom Extents.
